claims.location: source name, assay name, comment[data file], comment[technical replicate], and comment[fraction identifier], all rows
claims.value: 148 PRIDE RAW files mapped to 34 biological source identities, with SAX fractions and explicitly repeated injections preserved
claims.evidence: The PRIDE file inventory contains 148 RAW files. ProteomicsRAWfiles.xlsx maps every RAW filename to its Name, Group, MS Experiment, sample description, mouse identifier, age, sex, and animal count. Thirteen base/_SAX pairs have identical specimen description, mouse identifier(s), age, sex, and animal count and are modeled as one source each; distinct composite SAX pools remain separate. RAW suffixes and the sheet's '7 fractions SAX' designation establish fraction grouping, while duplicate source/fraction entries establish repeated injections.

claims.location: comment[fraction identifier] and comment[technical replicate] for 161222_QEx_LA_MS580_GC_01_pH3_02.raw
claims.evidence: The target is the second injection of the pH3 fraction for source DC_GC_03_05_SAX. Its sibling series establishes end=1, pH3=2, pH4=3, pH5=4, pH6=5, pH8=6, and pH11=7; the _pH3_02 filename preserves fraction 2 while technical replicate 2 distinguishes the reinjection.
The PRIDE project organism is Mus musculus and the associated study describes mouse intestinal cells.

claims.location: characteristics[organism part], characteristics[cell type], factor value[organism part], and factor value[cell type], all rows
claims.value: colon or ileum; epithelial cell or goblet cell
claims.evidence: The project title and description identify ileum and colon FACS-sorted Muc2-expressing and non-expressing cells. The deposited Group and Sample description fields explicitly distinguish DC versus Si8 and GC versus EC for each source; PRIDE also registers colon, ileum, goblet cell, and epithelial cell terms.

claims.location: characteristics[biological replicate] and characteristics[pooled sample], all rows
claims.value: specimen-consistent group-local biological replicate ordinals; pooled or not pooled
claims.evidence: Biological replicate ordinals are assigned to specimen identities within each biological group. For the 13 reviewed base/_SAX pairs, identical sample description, mouse identifier(s), age, sex, and animal count establish one specimen and therefore one biological-replicate value; technical-replicate identifiers preserve the separate unfractionated and SAX measurements. The sheet's Nr animals field explicitly states 1, Pool/pool of 2 animals, or Pool/pool of 4 animals.
The PRIDE description and Methods identify FACS-sorted epithelial-cell and goblet-cell populations.

claims.location: characteristics[developmental stage], all rows except source Si8_EC_01
claims.evidence: The deposited age values are 8, 9, or 11 weeks and were normalized to the controlled developmental-stage value adult. Si8_EC_01 has no deposited age and is explicitly recorded as not available.
Every mapped row in the deposited spreadsheet has Gender M.
PRIDE registers no disease and the deposited sample map provides no per-source disease status, so no normal or disease state was inferred.
The PRIDE data-processing protocol states that quantification used the MaxQuant LFQ protocol and describes no isotopic or isobaric label.

claims.location: comment[instrument], comment[proteomics data acquisition method], and comment[dissociation method], all rows
claims.value: Q Exactive; data-dependent acquisition; beam-type collision-induced dissociation
claims.evidence: The PRIDE record names the Q Exactive and describes top-12 precursor selection followed by fragmentation in the HCD collision cell.

The PRIDE sample-processing protocol states sequential Lys-C and trypsin digestion, and the data-processing protocol states full tryptic specificity. Trypsin is retained as the single v1.1.0 cleavage-agent value; the omitted preceding Lys-C step is documented as a limitation.

claims.location: three comment[modification parameters] columns, all rows
claims.value: Carbamidomethyl (C), Oxidation (M), and protein N-terminal Acetyl, all variable
claims.evidence: The PRIDE data-processing protocol explicitly lists carbamidomethylation of cysteine, methionine oxidation, and protein N-terminal acetylation as variable modifications.

limitations: The ms-proteomics v1.1.0 template permits only one cleavage-agent column. The sample preparation used sequential Lys-C and trypsin, so Lys-C cannot be represented alongside Trypsin without violating the declared template; reconciliation reports this as an incomplete cleavage-agent annotation.
The deposited map has no age for source Si8_EC_01; its developmental stage is therefore not available.
PRIDE and the deposited map provide no per-source disease status; disease is recorded as not available rather than inferred as normal.

Biological replicate values are deterministic group-local ordinals over biological specimen identities, not the submitter's mouse identifiers. Thirteen base/_SAX name pairs were unified only where all specimen fields match; composite SAX pools with different composition remain distinct.
Pooled status is represented, but individual contributing mouse identifiers remain only in the deposited spreadsheet.
